Given that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{72}∼N(11,{12}^{2})$ is a random sample of size $72$ from a normal population, calculate $P(10.75<\overset{―}{X}<11.3).$ *Hint: Value tables of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ are given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a normal population, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

then the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ has the distribution

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

Therefore, the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(11,\frac{{12}^{2}}{72}) \\  & ∼N(11,2).\end{aligned}
$$

We're required to find $P(10.75<\overset{―}{X}<11.3).$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(10.75<\overset{―}{X}<11.3) & =P(\frac{10.75-11}{\sqrt{2}}<Z<\frac{11.3-11}{\sqrt{2}}) \\  & =P(-0.18<Z<0.21) \\  & =Φ(0.21)-Φ(-0.18)\end{aligned}
$$

From the tables, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.21)=0.5832, \\ Φ(-0.18)=0.4286.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(10.75<\overset{―}{X}<11.3) & =Φ(0.21)-Φ(-0.18) \\  & =0.5832-0.4286 \\  & =0.1546.\end{aligned}
$$
